title: Hosted API: timeout amplification during tenant surge — customer mitigations and staged patch rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported elevated 5xx spikes and end-user timeouts during a morning surge on 2026-03-09. Symptoms looked like request retries amplifying load, intermittent KV cache thrashing for certain long-sequence requests, and upstream connection pool saturation on a subset of serving nodes. This ticket coordinates immediate mitigations, the root cause fix, a staged rollout, and customer communications.
steps_to_reproduce: Replay tenant traffic capture under load-synthesis with high concurrency and 8-16s model response tails
Trigger repeated client retries (exponential backoff disabled) to simulate misconfigured SDKs
Run long-context chat scenarios against model-variant 'gptx-large-v2' to observe KV cache eviction and recompute spikes
triage_logs: 2026-03-09T10:13Z - Incident channel created (#inc-hosted-5xx). Initial spike correlated to a 4x increase in request rate for 3 tenants.
2026-03-09T10:42Z - On-call applied tenant rate limit via edge policy; 5xx rate dropped ~30% for affected tenants.
2026-03-09T11:05Z - Observed connection_pool_wait_time increased on nodes serving shard us-west-2-a. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% to 57% for long-context requests.
root_cause: A confluence of factors: (1) customer SDKs were misconfigured and retried aggressively on transient latency causing retry amplification; (2) a recent kernel selection change for 'gptx-large-v2' increased memory working set for long sequences which reduced effective KV cache capacity causing expensive recomputes; (3) autoscaler thresholds were tuned to scale on CPU but not on connection queue length, causing delayed scale-up and connection pool saturation on several serving nodes. These combined to push nodes into long tail latencies and upstream 5xx errors as timeouts were hit.
immediate_mitigations: Applied tenant-level soft quota (edge policy) for the three worst-affected tenants — reduced concurrent inflight requests by 40%
Enabled conservative client-request header honor: we now short-circuit client-side retry headers that request <500ms backoff for hosted endpoints (edge guard) — temporary guard to stop amplification
Routed a subset of affected traffic to model-variant 'gptx-medium-v1' to reduce per-request memory footprint for 10% of traffic
Raised connection pool max size on us-west-2-a nodes by +50% as emergency knob
Published outbound customer advisory and scheduled 1:1 calls with top 5 impacted customers
long_term_fixes: Revert/adjust kernel-selection optimization that increased working set for long sequences or add memory-aware kernel selection logic
Instrument and enforce connection-queue-based autoscaling metric (queue_length + p95_latency) and adjust scaler to be more sensitive to sudden concurrency spikes
Implement server-side adaptive-backoff headers and a global circuit-breaker that can be toggled per-tenant
Ship client SDK patch (node/python/go) that implements recommended retry-backoff defaults and auto-detects hosted edge guard header to avoid amplification
Add KV cache eviction telemetry to runtime dashboards and create alerts when hit-rate drops >20% within 10 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Now) - Emergency mitigations applied (tenant quotas, routing to smaller variant, connection pool bump). Monitor for 8 hours.
Phase 1 - Deploy autoscaler change to staging and run 8-hour soak with synthetic tenant surge tests. Target date: 2026-03-16
Phase 2 - Canary rollout of kernel-selection fix to 3% traffic for 'gptx-large-v2' in us-west-2. Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit-rate, and 5xx counts for 72 hours.
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp to 25%/60%/100% with rollback windows and automated anomaly detection. Target date window: 2026-03-18 to 2026-03-20
Phase 4 - SDK patch release and request customers upgrade; set deprecation timeline for aggressive retry configs
monitoring_and_success_criteria: Sustained 5xx rate below baseline + 10% for affected tenants over 48 hours
KV cache hit-rate restored to >=90% for long-sequence traffic within 24 hours of kernel fix canary
Autoscaler responds to queue-length spikes within configured 60s window in canary environment
No customer escalations opened for same signature within 7 days after full rollout
customer_communications: Initial advisory sent 2026-03-09: 'We are investigating increased latency and risk of retries causing amplification; temporary quotas applied.' (sent to all affected contacts)
Follow-up 2026-03-10: scheduled live troubleshooting session with Enterprise customers A/B/C (calendar invites sent)
Post-fix summary and action items to be sent after full rollout with recommended SDK versions and configuration changes
